newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise, Lasmo vie for analysts' favour.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise, Lasmo vie for analysts' favour.

text.p: Enterprise Oil Plc may have been the FTSE 100's star performer last year but rival oil production and exploration firm Lasmo should catch up this year. At least that is what some analysts say.
Gone are the days that Lasmo's balance sheet was overstretched by the 1991 acquisition of Ultramar, they argue.

After trimming debt and cutting costs, the time has arrived fully to appreciate Lasmo's exciting prospects in Algeria and be prepared for other areas, such as Italy, to generate a positive news flow, the firm's supporters stress.
"Lasmo's success in turning its position around has not been fully recognised," said Richard Savage at Kleinwort Benson.
But there are plenty of other analysts who continue to favour Enterprise after it outperformed Lasmo by 22.8 percent in 1996, according to Reuters price performance data.
Enterprise investors have already stopped thinking about the company's recent past, dogged by its failed bid for Lasmo in 1994.
Instead, the spotlight last year abruptly turned to Enterprise's promising exploration prospects in Italy, Norway, Denmark and -- in the more distant future -- the Gulf of Mexico.
The company, privatised and floated in 1984, expects production to climb to 300,000 barrels per day by 1999 from a current 250,000 barrels.
Valued by the stock market at about 3.16 billion stg, Enterprise is the biggest British independent oil and exploration company.
Lasmo comes second, still well ahead of other British companies in the sector, with a market capitalisation of 2.39 billion stg.
The company expects to reach its 1997 production target of of approximately 200,000 barrels per day, an increase of 12 per cent over the expected 1996 level.
This year's level is forecast to be maintained for the next five years from the planned development of existing fields and discoveries under appraisal.

A common theme among industry watchers favouring Lasmo shares over Enterprise's is "valuation": these analysts believe Lasmo looks cheap compared with its rival, but stress Lasmo should not be considered a better company than Enterprise.
"We prefer Lasmo. It is mainly a ratings argument. Enterprise looks considerably more highly valued in terms of net asset value, or prospective cash flow multiple," said Colin Smith at BZW.

In contrast, the analysts supporting Enterprise usually come up with fundamental reasons backing their stance. They say their favourite has a lower cost base and more exploration potential than Lasmo.

"Lasmo has its crown jewel in Algeria but it remains to be seen how quickly they can get all that oil flowing to the bottom line. I'd much rather play Enterprise which has a more steady growth potential," said Shawn Reynolds at Lehman Brothers.
"Enterprise has lower finding costs, has lower operating costs. At all levels, it continues to be better than Lasmo," he added.

It may not mean much yet, but so far this year Enterprise has underperformed Lasmo by 7.7 percent. Enterprise was down 2-1/2 pence to 633-1/2 in late Friday morning trade while Lasmo eased two pence to 249.
